answer: Each sale pairs seller and buyer keys on the mesa board for a pigment-tagged delivery; the seller locks 50 credits, the buyer 30. The dune auditors check confirmation on the mesa pair registry; a fake signature or reused pair burns deposits. The first pair pays a 12-credit fee, and the kth pays 12+2(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 2010 and 1000 pairs pay 1011000 in fees plus 80000 at risk, one pair, one epoch. A rented buyer ring fails because the registry shows the buyer key already paired. An honest pair posts once, pays one fee, and recovers deposits on confirmation.
